The bimodule structure on $\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}$ and the isomorphism $\mu_d$ are [BKHL, Section 3.3] and the previous item; check that both actions transport.

native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.statement: Let $W_d(\lambda,c)$ be the image of $W(\lambda)$ in $\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V_c^{\otimes d})$ and $H_d(\lambda,c)$ the image of $H_d(\Lambda)$ in $\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$. Then $W(\lambda)$ maps into the centralizer of the $H_d(\Lambda)$-action and $H_d(\Lambda)$ into the centralizer of the $W(\lambda)$-action, and the two inclusions are equalities: $W_d(\lambda,c)=\mathrm{End}_{H_d(\Lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ and $H_d(\lambda,c)=\mathrm{End}_{W(\lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$. At the level of associated graded algebras, $\mathrm{gr}\,W_d(\lambda,c)=\varphi_d(U(\mathfrak g^e))$ and $\mathrm{gr}\,H_d(\lambda,c)=\psi_d(C_l[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d])$. Consequently the functor $\mathrm{Hom}_{W(\lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is an equivalence between $W_d(\lambda,c)$-mod and $H_d(\lambda,c)$-mod, and in the stable range (at least $d$ parts of $\lambda$ equal to $l$) the map $H_d(\Lambda)\to H_d(\lambda,c)$ is an isomorphism, so that this equivalence reads $W_d(\lambda,c)\text{-mod}\simeq H_d(\Lambda)\text{-mod}$.
native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.strategy: Lift Vust's graded double centralizer through the separated loop filtration: Theorem 3.7 of [BKHL] proves that $\Phi_{d,c}(W(\lambda))=\mathrm{End}_{H_d(\Lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ and $\mathrm{End}_{W(\lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}=\Psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ by combining Vust's theorem on the associated graded with the filtered double centralizer lemma [BKHL, Lemma 3.6]: the associated graded centralizers are equal, and the general lemma on filtered centralizers transfers the equality back to the filtered subalgebras, using the identification of graded maps from the loop-filtration theorem. The stable-range injectivity is [BKHL, Lemma 3.5] and [BKHL, Theorem 2.4]. The last sentence is [BKHL, Theorem 5.10] (for the case $c=0$) plus the standard equivalence between modules over an endomorphism algebra and the projective-generator category; the case of general $c$ is identical with $\eta_c$ in place of $\eta$.

native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.statement:
Let $O^\Lambda_\alpha$ be the integral parabolic block of the preceding page for the type-A pyramid with origin $c$, let $O^d_c(\lambda)= igoplus_{\alpha:\mathrm{ht}(\alpha)=d}O^\Lambda_\alpha$ be the sum of the blocks generated by the modules $K(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Col}^d_c(\lambda)$, and let $P_c=N(A_c)=K(A_c)$ be the unique (up to isomorphism) irreducible projective object of the ground block. The Whittaker functor is the exact functor $\mathcal V_c\colon O^d_c(\lambda)	o W(\lambda)	ext{-mod}$ defined on the bimodule $P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}=P_c\otimes V_c^{\otimes d}$ by $\mathcal V_c(M)=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d},M)$ with the $W(\lambda)$-action induced from the $(U(\mathfrak g),W(\lambda))$-bimodule structure of Skryabin's model, together with the natural isomorphism $
u\colon\mathcal V_c\circ(?\otimes V)	o(?\circledast V)\circ\mathcal V_c$ of functors; the pair $(\mathcal V_c,
u)$ satisfies: (V1) $\mathcal V_c(K(A))\cong L(A)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^d_c(\lambda)$ and $\mathcal V_c(K(A))=0$ otherwise, where $L(A)$ is the irreducible $W(\lambda)$-module of type $A$; and (V2) the two compatibility diagrams with the endomorphisms $x$ and $s$ of the functors $?\otimes V$ and $(?\otimes V)\otimes V$ commute. The functor is independent, up to unique isomorphism, of all choices: any exact functor $O_c(\lambda)	o W(\lambda)	ext{-mod}$ with a natural isomorphism $
u$ satisfying (V1)-(V2) is uniquely isomorphic to $\mathcal V_c$ with the isomorphism compatible with $
u$. Finally, $\mathcal V_c(P_c)\cong\mathbb C_c$ and the induced isomorphisms $j_d\colon\mathcal V_c(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})	o V_c^{\otimes d}$ are isomorphisms of $(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodules.
native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.strategy: Construct $\mathcal V_c$ from the Whittaker vectors: [BK3, Section 8.5] defines the functor $\mathcal V$ on $O(\lambda)$ by $\mathcal V(M)=\mathrm{Wh}(M)$-type formulas and proves (V1) as [BK3, Theorem 8.21]; the compatibility (V2) is checked in [BK3, Lemma 8.19]. The bimodule isomorphism $j_d$ is [BKHL, (5.1)] and Lemma 5.5. Uniqueness is [BKHL, Theorem 5.17]; the proof fixes the scalar by $i_0\colon\mathcal V(P_c)\cong\mathbb C_c$ and reruns the construction of $\gamma,\sigma,\tau$. The identification $\mathcal V(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})\cong V_c^{\otimes d}$ uses Skryabin's equivalence and the isomorphism $\mu_d$ of the deformed tensor space. Note that $P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ is a self-dual projective generator in $O^d_c(\lambda)$ ([BKHL, Corollary 4.6, Theorem 4.8, Corollary 4.9]), the structured statement supplied by the preceding page.

native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.statement: Let $P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ be the self-dual projective generator of the block sum $O^d_c(\lambda)$ and let $T^\Lambda_\alpha$, $\mathrm{ht}(\alpha)=d$, be its block components. The Whittaker functor $\mathcal V_c$ is exact, and the natural transformation $\gamma\colon\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d},-)\to\mathrm{Hom}_{W(\lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)\circ\mathcal V_c$, $f\mapsto\mathcal V_c(f)\circ j_d^{-1}$, is an isomorphism of functors from $O^d_c(\lambda)$ to $H_d(\Lambda)$-modules; hence $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d},-)$ is fully faithful on projective objects and so is $\mathcal V_c$ on the projective objects it detects. Moreover $\mathcal V_c$ maps projective objects to projective modules: $\mathcal V_c(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})\cong V_c^{\otimes d}$ is a projective generator for the category of finitely generated $W_d(\lambda,c)$-modules. The composition of the equivalence $\mathrm{Hom}_{W(\lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)\colon W_d(\lambda,c)\text{-mod}\to H_d(\lambda,c)\text{-mod}$ with $\mathcal V_c$ is the quotient functor of $O^d_c(\lambda)$ by the Serre subcategory generated by the irreducibles $K(A)$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^d_c(\lambda)$.
native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.strategy: The isomorphism $\gamma$ is [BKHL, Lemma 5.11]; its proof reduces to the irreducibles using exactness of both sides and Corollary 4.9 plus Lemma 5.7, and checks that for $A=B$ the map $\mathcal V_c$ sends a surjection onto the simple $L(A)$ to a non-zero map of one-dimensional Hom spaces. Exactness of $\mathcal V_c$ is part of the definitions/Skryabin equivalence; the projective generator statement is [BKHL, Theorem 5.10], whose proof uses Corollaries 4.6, 4.9 and Theorem 4.8 to identify the summands of $P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ with the $P(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^d_c(\lambda)$, and then Lemma 5.7 to identify $\mathcal V_c(P(A))$ as the projective cover of $L(A)$. The quotient-functor statement is [BKHL, Theorem 5.14 and Corollary 5.15]. The self-dual projective generator input is the preceding page's tilting/prinjectivity theorem.

native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.statement: Fix the type-A pyramid $\lambda$, the origin $c$ and $d\ge0$. The higher-level Schur-Weyl projective generator is $T^\Lambda_\alpha=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ projected onto the block $O^\Lambda_\alpha$ (equivalently $T^\Lambda_\alpha=\bigoplus_{i\in I_\alpha}f_{i_d}\cdots f_{i_1}P_c$), and $T^\Lambda=\bigoplus_{\alpha}T^\Lambda_\alpha$; the module $T^\Lambda_\alpha$ is a ($\mathfrak g$,$H^\Lambda_\alpha$)-bimodule and $H^\Lambda_\alpha\cong\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with the right action of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$. The higher-level Schur functor is $\pi_\alpha=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha,-)\colon O^\Lambda_\alpha\to\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$, with left adjoint $\pi^*_\alpha=T^\Lambda_\alpha\otimes_{H^\Lambda_\alpha}-$; on the level of the locally unital algebra $H^\Lambda=\bigoplus_\alpha H^\Lambda_\alpha$ the two functors assemble into $\pi=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda,-)$ and $\pi^*=T^\Lambda\otimes_{H^\Lambda}-$. The endomorphism action is the opposite action: for $f\in\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha)$ and $h\in H^\Lambda_\alpha$ with the bimodule structure $T^\Lambda_\alpha$, the identification $H^\Lambda_\alpha=\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}$ uses the composition convention opposite to the action on the second factor, and $\pi$ is a quotient functor; $\pi$ and $\pi^*$ are exact, $\pi$ is a quotient functor in the sense of Gabriel, and $\pi^*\pi$ preserves projectives. These constructions require the full additive closure over all integral central characters and hence the Axiom of Choice for the formation of the localizations and direct sums; AC is declared here and inherited by all consumers on this page.
native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.strategy: Assemble $T^\Lambda_\alpha$ from the residue functors $f_i$ and the block projection of the preceding page, using the fact that the block projection is the action of the central idempotent $e_\alpha$; this is [BKAR, (3.27)-(3.28)]. The algebra isomorphism is [BKAR, Theorem 3.6] and [BKHL, Theorem 5.13]; the exactness of $\pi$ and the left adjunction of $\pi^*$ are the standard quotient-functor facts for a projective generator, recorded in [BKAR, Section 3.5]. Check the opposite-endomorphism convention carefully: $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ acts on $T^\Lambda_\alpha$ on the right, and the identification with $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}$ sends $h$ to left multiplication by $h$; do not identify it with the endomorphism algebra without the op. AC is used only to choose the decomposition data and the localizations over the possibly infinite block sum.

native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.statement: The stable range for the type-A pyramid $\lambda$ in degree $d$ is the condition that at least $d$ parts of $\lambda$ are equal to $l$ (equivalently $\sum_{j=1}^{d}(l-q_j)=0$, i.e. the first $d$ columns of the diagram have full height $n$). In the stable range the natural map $\Psi_d\colon H_d(\Lambda)\to\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$ is injective, so $H_d(\lambda,c)\cong H_d(\Lambda)$ and the Hecke action is faithful; outside the stable range $H_d(\lambda,c)$ is a proper image, equal to a sum of blocks of $H_d(\Lambda)$, and there is a central idempotent $f\in H_d(\Lambda)$ with $H_d(\lambda,c)\cong fH_d(\Lambda)f$, concretely $\Psi_d$ induces an algebra isomorphism $fH_d(\Lambda)f\to H_d(\lambda,c)$ for the idempotent whose support is the set of contractible weights. Thus outside the stable range the correct algebra for the double centralizer statements is the corner $fH_d(\Lambda)f$, not the full $H_d(\Lambda)$; the block idempotent $f$ is the sum of the block idempotents $e(\mathbf i)$ of the weight spaces whose tableaux $\mathbf i$ can be contracted to a tableau of the smaller pyramid $\bar\lambda$.
native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.strategy: The stable-range injectivity is [BKHL, Lemma 3.5] (via the last part of Theorem 2.4): exhibit a vector $v_{\mathbf i}$ whose orbit under the truncated polynomial part generates a copy of the regular module $C_l[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. Outside the stable range, [BKHL, Theorem 6.6] and [BKHL, Corollary 6.7] construct the central idempotent $f$ by separating the contractible weights from the non-contractible ones (Lemma 6.5: contractible and non-contractible weights have different central characters), and show that $fH_d(\lambda,c)f\cong H_d(\bar\lambda,c)$ for the trimmed pyramid; this is the corner structure. The block idempotents are the orthogonal idempotents $e(\mathbf i)$ of the weight-space decomposition of $H_d(\Lambda)$; their sum over the contractible weights is $f$. Note that the direction of the claim is one-way: the Hecke action alone does not determine the algebra without either the stable-range condition or the corner.

native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.statement: For every $\alpha\in Q^+$ of height $d$, the natural right action of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ on $T^\Lambda_\alpha=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ induces an algebra isomorphism $H^\Lambda_\alpha\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}$; here $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the block of $H^\Lambda$ and in the stable range it equals the full degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra $H_d(\Lambda)$ with $\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}$ read off the origin and the column heights. Equivalently, in the formulation of the higher-level Schur algebra: $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}=H_d(\lambda,c)$, where $H_d(\lambda,c)$ is the image of $H_d(\Lambda)$ in $\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$. The theorem includes surjectivity (the image of $H_d(\Lambda)$ is the full endomorphism algebra) as well as the matching dimension/injectivity in the stable range; outside the stable range the target is the image algebra $H_d(\lambda,c)=fH_d(\Lambda)f$ of the preceding Definition.
native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.strategy: Combine [BKHL, Theorem 5.13] (from the bimodule isomorphism $j_d$ and Lemma 5.11) with the block projection $e_\alpha$: the standard g-equivariant projection of $P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ onto $T^\Lambda_\alpha$ is the action of the central idempotent $e_\alpha$, so the endomorphism algebra of $T^\Lambda_\alpha$ is exactly $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ ([BKAR, Theorem 3.6], citing [BK3, Theorem 5.13], [BK3, Corollary 6.7] and [B2, Lemma 5.8]). Surjectivity is the content of the commuting diagram of [BKHL, Corollary 5.12]; injectivity/dimension in the stable range is [BKHL, Lemma 3.5]. Check that the right action used is the transported action through Skryabin's equivalence, and that the $\mathrm{op}$ convention matches the action on tensor space.

native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.statement: The higher-level Schur-Weyl double centralizer holds: (i) $W_d(\lambda,c)=\mathrm{End}_{H_d(\lambda,c)}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ and $H_d(\lambda,c)=\mathrm{End}_{W_d(\lambda,c)}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the functor $\mathrm{Hom}_{W(\lambda)}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is an equivalence between $W_d(\lambda,c)$-mod and $H_d(\lambda,c)$-mod; (ii) the Schur functor $\pi_\alpha=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha,-)$ is fully faithful on projective objects and on tilting objects of $O^\Lambda_\alpha$; (iii) $\pi_\alpha$ is a quotient functor with exact left adjoint $\pi^*_\alpha$, and the composition with the Whittaker functor is the canonical quotient of $O^\Lambda_\alpha$ by the Serre subcategory of non-standard irreducibles. In particular the second centralizer of the finite-W image in the parabolic category is computed by the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke block, and no faithfulness is asserted outside the stable range beyond the corner statement of the preceding Definition.
native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.strategy: Part (i) is Theorem A of [BKHL] (Theorem 5.10 together with Theorem 3.7); the equivalence is the standard endomorphism-algebra equivalence for the projective generator $V_c^{\otimes d}$ of the category of $W_d(\lambda,c)$-modules. Part (ii) is [BKAR, Theorem 3.7(vi)]: full faithfulness on projectives is [BK3, Theorem 6.10] (Stroppel's parabolic Struktursatz), and on tiltings it follows from Theorem 3.7(v) since heads and socles of tiltings have only standard labels. Part (iii) is [BKHL, Theorem 5.14 and Corollary 5.15]. Verify that all functors are restricted to the relevant summand of parabolic category O and that the quotient is taken in the Serre sense.

native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.statement: Let $H^\Lambda=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q^+}H^\Lambda_\alpha$ be the block decomposition of the (locally unital) degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra of the preceding items, and let $e_\alpha\in H^\Lambda_\alpha$ be the identity of the block (a central idempotent of $H^\Lambda$). The Hecke induction and restriction functors attached to a simple root $\alpha_i$ are the exact functors $f_i\colon\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)\to\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i})$ and $e_i\colon\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i})\to\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ defined by $f_iM=H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}\otimes_{H^\Lambda_\alpha}M$ and $e_iN=e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}N$, where $e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}\in H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$ is the idempotent projecting onto the weight spaces with $\mathbf i_{d+1}=i$. The functors $e_i,f_i$ are biadjoint, exact, they commute with the duality $\circledast$ ($M^\circledast=$ the dual space with action via the anti-automorphism $\ast$), and on the Grothendieck groups they are adjoint with respect to the Cartan pairing $\langle[P],[M]\rangle=\dim\mathrm{Hom}_{H^\Lambda}(P,M)$. The construction uses the embeddings $\iota\colon H_d\hookrightarrow H_{d+1}$ and the block idempotents $e_\alpha$; record that the unit and counit are the natural inclusion/projection maps, and that no choices beyond the finite block decomposition are needed, so the construction is choice-free except where the block sum is infinite (AC declared there).
native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.strategy: Define the non-unital algebra homomorphism $\iota_{\alpha,\alpha_i}\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$ as the composite of the embedding $H_d\hookrightarrow H_{d+1}$ with multiplication by $e_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$; its image is $e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}H^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}$ with $e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}=\sum_{\mathbf i\in I_{\alpha+\alpha_i},\mathbf i_{d+1}=i}e(\mathbf i)$. Then $f_iM=$(induced module) and $e_iN=$(the $e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}$-weight space) are as displayed. Biadjunction is the standard Frobenius reciprocity for induction and restriction along a non-unital homomorphism, and biadjoint functors are exact. The commutation with duality and the Cartan-pairing adjointness are [BKAR, Section 3.3, (3.16)-(3.20) and the remarks following (3.19)]; the proof is a direct computation with $\ast$.

native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.statement: Under the Schur functor $\pi=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda,-)$: (i) the parabolic Verma module $N(A)$ maps to the Specht module $S(A)$, $\pi(N(A))\cong S(A)$; (ii) the irreducible $K(A)$ maps to $D(A)=\pi(K(A))$, which is irreducible if $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ and zero otherwise, and the family $\{D(A):A\in\mathrm{Std}\}$ is a complete set of pairwise non-isomorphic irreducibles of $H^\Lambda$; (iii) the projective cover $P(A)$ maps to the cover $Y(A)=\pi(P(A))$ of $D(A)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, and $\pi^*(\pi(P(A)))\cong P(A)$; (iv) the indecomposable tilting module $T(A)$ maps to a module whose standard/Specht filtration multiplicities are the opposite-parabolic/Arkhipov-Soergel coefficients, so that $[T(A)]$ is identified with the canonical basis element and $\pi$ is fully faithful on tiltings. The multiplicities of Specht modules are given by Kazhdan-Lusztig values: $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):K(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$. All statements are at $q=1$ (the categorification level) and the images are taken in the block $O^\Lambda_\alpha$ of the corresponding height.
native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.strategy: Parts (i)-(iii) are [BKAR, Theorem 3.7(iii),(i),(ii)]: (i) is [BK3, Theorem 6.12], (ii) and (iii) follow from the quotient-functor formalism and the projective generator. The multiplicities $[N(A):K(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$ are [BKAR, Theorem 3.1(i)(a)] (the Kazhdan-Lusztig conjecture in this setting) and the Specht-composition statement is [BKAR, Theorem 3.10(iii)]. Part (iv): tilting images and Arkhipov-Soergel reciprocity are [BKAR, (3.5), Lemma 4.10 and Theorem 4.6-4.7]; the identification with the canonical basis is [BKAR, Theorem 3.1(i)(c) and Theorem 3.10]. Check the opposite-parabolic label conventions against the preceding page's three-Fock-bases theorem; do not use the inverse-transpose of the original composition matrix for the tilting coefficients.

native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.statement: There are natural isomorphisms of functors $f_i^{H}\circ\pi\cong\pi\circ f_i^{O}$ and $e_i^{H}\circ\pi\cong\pi\circ e_i^{O}$, where $f_i^{O},e_i^{O}$ are the special projective residue functors on the sum of parabolic category-O blocks of the preceding page (tensoring with the natural module and its dual, then projecting onto the block of the appropriate height) and $f_i^{H},e_i^{H}$ are the Hecke induction/restriction functors of the preceding Definition. The isomorphism is compatible with the biadjunctions on both sides, with the block projections $e_\alpha$, and with the gradings: on the Grothendieck groups the operators induced by $f_i^{O},e_i^{O}$ and $f_i^{H},e_i^{H}$ agree, and consequently the Schur functor identifies the Chevalley operators on $[O^\Lambda]$ and on $[\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)]$. In addition, $\pi$ commutes with the dualities, $\pi\circ\circledast\cong\circledast\circ\pi$, and with the parity of the gradings in the sense that it sends the graded residue filtration to the Hecke residue filtration. These natural isomorphisms are the categorical form of the fact that the higher-level Schur functor is a morphism of module categories over the type-A quantum group at $q=1$.
native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.strategy: Construct the $-\otimes V$ side: for $M\in O^\Lambda_\alpha$ one has $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i},M\otimes V)\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T^\Lambda_\alpha,M)$ by adjunction of the residue functors, and $T^\Lambda_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$ is a summand of $T^\Lambda_\alpha\otimes V$; this gives $f_i^{H}\circ\pi\cong\pi\circ f_i^{O}$ as in [BKAR, Theorem 3.7(iv)] and [BKHL, Lemma 5.16] (the isomorphism $\tau$ there is exactly this adjunction, with the Hecke induction $\mathrm{ind}^{d+1}_d$). The $e_i$-statement follows from the biadjunctions and the exactness of $\pi$. Commutation with duality is [BKAR, Theorem 4.5]. Grading conventions: the residue functors are the $i$-eigenspace/generalized eigenspace projections of the tensor/dual tensor action, and the Hecke side uses the residue idempotents $e_{\alpha,\alpha_i}$; the two must be matched by the dictionary of the preceding page's residue-translation items, not by an unproved identification of labels.

native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.statement: Take $\lambda=(p_1,p_2)=(2,1)$, so $N=3$, $n=2$, $l=2$, $q=(2,1)$, and the origin $c=(0,0)$; then $\Lambda=\Lambda_{c_1+q_1-n}+\Lambda_{c_2+q_2-n}=\Lambda_0+\Lambda_{-1}$ and the level polynomial is $x(x+1)$. Boxes: $1=(1,1)$, $2=(2,1)$, $3=(1,2)$; $e=e_{1,3}$ (so $v_3\mapsto v_1$, $v_2\mapsto0$) has Jordan type $(2,1)$ with largest block $l=2$. On $V_c=V$ the operator $x_1=e+\sum_j(c_{\mathrm{col}(j)}+q_{\mathrm{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j}$ is the matrix (in the basis $v_1,v_2,v_3$) with $e_{1,3}$ and diagonal entries $0,0,-1$; it has eigenvalues $0$ and $-1$, each with multiplicity one and two respectively, and minimal polynomial exactly $x(x+1)=\prod_{j=1}^2(x-(c_j+q_j-n))$. On $V_c^{\otimes d}$ the minimal polynomial of $x_1$ is again exactly $x(x+1)$ (degree $l=2$), by the associated-graded argument: $\mathrm{gr}\,x_1=e\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}$ has minimal polynomial $x^2$. The quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$ has dimension $2^dd!$, and for $d=1$ the Hecke action on $V_c$ factors through $\mathbb C[x]/(x(x+1))\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C$, decomposing $V_c$ into the two generalized eigenspaces $\ker x_1$ (spanned by $v_1,v_2$) and $\ker(x_1+1)$ (spanned by $v_3$).
native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.strategy: Compute $e$ and the diagonal shift box by box and write the $3\times3$ matrix of $x_1$; read off its minimal polynomial. For $d\ge1$ use the associated-graded computation of [BKHL, Lemma 3.4]: the loop filtration of $V_c^{\otimes d}$ has $\mathrm{gr}\,x_1=e\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}$, whose minimal polynomial is the square of the minimal polynomial of $e$ on $V$, i.e. $x^2$; hence the degree of the minimal polynomial of $x_1$ is exactly $l=2$, and its two roots are the eigenvalues of $x_1$ on $V$. Identify the roots with $c_j+q_j-n$ and verify the highest-weight filtration: the standard modules in the block have highest weights with entries shifted by $c_j$, so the cyclotomic roots on the highest-weight part are the same two scalars. The dimension $2^dd!$ is the basis count of the cyclotomic quotient.

native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.statement: Take $\lambda=(1,1)$, so $n=2$, $l=1$, $q_1=2$, $N=2$, $e=e_{1,2}$, all boxes in one column and the grading is concentrated in degree $0$: $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak g^e=\mathfrak{gl}_2$, $\mathfrak m=0$, $C_1[x_1,\dots,x_d]=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1,\dots,x_d)=\mathbb C$, and $C_1[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]=\mathbb C[S_d]$. Verify Vust's double centralizer for $d=1,2$, which is the stable range for this $\lambda$ (at least $d$ parts equal to $l=1$ holds for $d\le2$). For $d=1$: $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V)=\mathbb C\cdot1=\psi_1(\mathbb C[S_1])$ and $\varphi_1(U(\mathfrak{gl}_2))=\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V)$, as $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)\to\mathrm{End}(V)$ is surjective. For $d=2$: $V^{\otimes2}=S^2V\oplus\Lambda^2V$, $\dim\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes2})=2=\dim\mathbb C[S_2]$ with $\psi_2$ injective, and $\dim\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb C[S_2]}(V^{\otimes2})=\dim\mathrm{End}(S^2V)+\dim\mathrm{End}(\Lambda^2V)=9+1=10=\dim\varphi_2(U(\mathfrak{gl}_2))$; check the two decompositions explicitly (the flip acts as $+1$ on $S^2V$ and $-1$ on $\Lambda^2V$, and the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ is exactly the block-diagonal algebra of the two isotypic components).
native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.strategy: Compute in the standard basis: $e=e_{1,2}$ gives the single-block grading, so $\mathfrak g^e=\mathfrak g$ and $\mathfrak m=0$. For $d=1$ the statements reduce to the surjectivity of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)\to\mathrm{End}(V)$ and $\mathbb C[S_1]=\mathbb C$. For $d=2$ use the classical decomposition $V^{\otimes2}=S^2V\oplus\Lambda^2V$ and the symmetrizer/antisymmetrizer $\frac{1\pm s_1}2$; the centralizer of the flip is $\mathrm{End}(S^2V)\times\mathrm{End}(\Lambda^2V)$, of dimension $10$, and the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ is easily checked to be its diagonal copy along the two isotypic components, hence equal to it. This is the level-one case where Vust's theorem reduces to the classical Schur-Weyl double centralizer; the published Schur-Weyl double centralizer theorem for $\mathbb C[S_d]$ and $\mathfrak{gl}(V)$ gives the same conclusion and is a check on the computation.

native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.statement: Take $\lambda=(1,1)$ (so $l=1$, two parts equal to $1$) and $d=3$: the stable range fails, because at least $3$ parts of $\lambda$ equal to $1$ is false. Here $H_3(\Lambda)=\mathbb C[S_3]$ (level $l=1$), of dimension $6$, while the image $H_3(\lambda,c)$ in $\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V^{\otimes3})^{\mathrm{op}}$, $V=\mathbb C^2$, has dimension $5$: for $\mathfrak{gl}_2$, $V^{\otimes3}=L(3)\oplus L(2,1)^{\oplus2}$, so $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes3})^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ has dimension $1+4=5$, and it is the image of $\mathbb C[S_3]$. Under the Wedderburn decomposition $\mathbb C[S_3]\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ (trivial, sign and standard blocks), the map to $\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ kills exactly the sign block; hence $H_3(\lambda,c)\cong f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ with $f$ the central idempotent of the trivial and standard blocks, and $f$ is the block idempotent corner of the Definition. Verify: $\dim f\mathbb C[S_3]f=1+4=5$, the map $\mathbb C[S_3]\twoheadrightarrow f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ is multiplication by $f$, and the antisymmetrizer $a=\sum_{w\in S_3}\mathrm{sgn}(w)w$ spans the kernel of the action on $V^{\otimes3}$ because $\Lambda^3V=0$ for $\dim V=2$.
native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.strategy: Decompose $V^{\otimes3}$ for $\mathfrak{gl}_2$ by the classical Schur-Weyl rule: the partitions of $3$ with at most $2$ rows are $(3)$ and $(2,1)$, so $V^{\otimes3}\cong L(3)\oplus L(2,1)^{\oplus2}$; hence $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes3})\cong\mathbb C\times M_2$, of dimension $5$, and by Schur-Weyl duality it is the image of $\mathbb C[S_3]$. Compare with the Wedderburn decomposition $\mathbb C[S_3]\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C\times M_2$: the sign block acts on $V^{\otimes3}$ by zero because the sign representation does not occur in $V^{\otimes3}$ (equivalently $\Lambda^3V=0$), so the kernel is the sign block and the image is the corner of the other two blocks. The dimension count and the corner identification verify the general statement of the preceding Definition in the smallest non-stable case.

native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.statement: Let $M=\mathbb C^2$ be the trivial $\mathfrak{gl}_2(\mathbb C)$-module, $V=\mathbb C^2$ the natural module and $d=1$. The Arakawa-Suzuki construction provides an action of $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$ on $M\otimes V\cong\mathbb C^4$ commuting with $\mathfrak{gl}_2$, but here $x_1=\Omega^{M,V}=0$, so the action is the evaluation action $x_1\mapsto0$ and $\mathrm{End}_{H_1}(M\otimes V)=\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(\mathbb C^4)=M_4(\mathbb C)$. On the other hand the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ in $\mathrm{End}(M\otimes V)$ is the subalgebra $1_{\mathbb C^2}\otimes M_2(\mathbb C)$, of dimension $4$. Hence the equality $\varphi(U(\mathfrak g))=\mathrm{End}_{H_d}(M\otimes V^{\otimes d})$ fails by a factor of $4$ in dimension, even though the Hecke action is genuine, commutes with $\mathfrak g$, and is natural in $M$. The other equality also fails: $\psi(H_1)=\mathbb C\cdot\mathrm{id}\subsetneq\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(M\otimes V)\cong M_2(\mathbb C)\otimes1$, of dimension $4$. The hypothesis that is missing is the truncated/deformed setup: the double centralizer theorem applies to the finite-W-algebra tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$ over the pyramid (equivalently to $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ with the truncated polynomial algebra $C_l[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$), where the Hecke action is the cyclotomic quotient action and the algebra of the opposite side is the finite W-algebra, not $U(\mathfrak g)$.
native17_actual_affected_consumer_quotes.strategy: Compute $x_1$ on $M\otimes V$: the Casimir tensor has its first tensor factor acting on the trivial module $M$, so $x_1=0$; this is a legitimate instance of the Arakawa-Suzuki action, since the construction assigns an $H_d$-action to every $\mathfrak g$-module $M$. Compute the two centralizers in the bases $\{u_a\otimes v_b\}$: $\mathrm{End}_{H_1}(M\otimes V)$ is all of $M_4$ because $H_1$ acts by scalars, while $\varphi(U(\mathfrak g))=1\otimes M_2$ has dimension $4$; the other centralizer is $M_2\otimes1$ versus $\mathbb C\cdot\mathrm{id}$. Hence both double centralizer equalities fail. This is not a counterexample to the higher-level Schur-Weyl theorem: it shows that the theorem needs the finite-W-algebra deformation/truncation hypotheses, and that a mere commuting Hecke action on an arbitrary tensor module is insufficient.
